habit_scope: traditional / IRC-table path (AF&PA Platform Frame; HUD RSDG §§1.1, 5.4.2). Still fully legal. Volume habit is I-joist (D4).
how_it_is_done: Sill/anchors on the cured wall (AF&PA Sills; ORNL notes 11, 13, 31). Embed D2 follow adopted code (c-P05-D2-sill-bolt-embed).

Girders: solid, built-up nailed, or glulam (AF&PA Beams); steel W house beam / flitch / box beam as girder alts (HUD §5.4.3) — girder only, not a floor habit. Bar joists rejected. D5: AF&PA two rows 20d at 32 in o.c. vs HUD 10d staggered 12 in o.c. Keep both; do not mix on one beam; follow NDS/IRC (c-P07-D5-girder-nailing). Joints over supports; adjacent joints ≥16 in apart (AF&PA). Bearing ≥4 in (AF&PA).
Joists crown up; two toenails or hangers. Bearing ≥1½ in on wood/metal, ≥3 in on masonry (AF&PA). Do not apply this 1½ in under I-joists (D10 is the I-joist rule).

Prefer framing into girder sides (ledger, hangers, or hangers to steel) vs sitting on top to reduce shrinkage stack (AF&PA). Platform frame: first-floor joists fully sheathed, then walls tilt up (AF&PA Fig 1) — all four sources agree platform is the erection method.
Rim/band nailing. Openings: double trimmer/header when header >4 ft; hangers when header >6 ft or tails >12 ft (AF&PA).

Bridging D3 / c-P07-D3-sawn-bridging: skip intermediate bridging if subfloor and band are well nailed unless depth/thickness >6 or twisting is a known problem (then 8 ft, 1x4 or solid 2x) vs HUD NAHB 1961 negligible for 2x6–2x12 with panel subfloor, NDS 4.4.1 still ≤8 ft on 2x10/2x12. Keep both. Not a separate method. Does not apply to I-joists.

Sawn hole/notch rules only (AF&PA Notching): no holes/notches in middle third; outer-third notch ≤1/6 depth; end notch ≤1/4; hole ≤1/3 depth and ≥2 in from edges. Do not mix with I-joist web-hole tables.

Subfloor: panels long way across joists, continuous ≥2 spans, ~1/8 in gap (AF&PA Sub-flooring). T&G 5/8 or 3/4 typical (HUD §5.4.4). Glue + nails recommended by AF&PA (squeaks) and HUD (stiffness) — not the PJI catalog-span requirement. Fastener grid 6 in edge / 12 in field (HUD Table 5.5). IRC/sawn tables ~L/360 live (HUD Table 5.4).
Crawl clearances 12 in earth-to-girder, 18 in earth-to-joist (AF&PA). Floor in before significant basement backfill (HUD §4.5).

tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources. Named: hangers as an opening/girder option (AF&PA).
inspection_hold_points: Sawn hole/notch rules — do not use I-joist tables.
Girder nail schedule is one schedule per beam (D5).
Floor in before significant basement backfill (HUD §4.5).
when_this_beats_habit: Still the IRC-table path when the job wants any lumberyard stock, no proprietary ESR, or conventional spans. Legal everywhere these books reach. Not the volume habit (D4).
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Long spans / fewer interior bearings — that is the floor-truss alt. Mixing I-joist hole or bearing rules. SOG South — no joist package. Balloon frame is legacy (AF&PA Balloon; HUD §1.1), not this method. Plank-and-beam points to AF&PA WCD 4, not detailed here — not a Method.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They learned it — it is the old habit. What changed is volume share, not legality.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Sawn vs I-joist is a permit-gate framing choice. Engineer when tables fail (HUD).
risk_if_swapped_late: Sawn vs I-joist after permit changes spans, hangers, hole rules, and subfloor glue spec. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Regular 2x joists, still in the code tables. Crown up, sit them 1½ inches on wood, do not notch the middle third. Bridging is optional or at 8 feet depending which book you follow — do not fight it on the job, pick one. This is not the volume floor anymore, but it is still legal. Do not use these hole rules on I-joists.
spanish_summary: Viguetas de 2x de siempre, todavía en las tablas del código. Corona arriba, 1½ pulgadas de apoyo en madera, sin recortes en el tercio de en medio. El bridging o se omite o va a 8 pies según el libro — no mezcle. Ya no es lo que más se usa, pero es legal. No aplique estas reglas de huecos a las viguetas en I.

fastener_schedule.source: ORNL notes 13/31; AF&PA Sills. Embed D2 both variants (AF&PA ≥6 in CIP / ≥15 in block vs ORNL most codes ≥7 in / some 15 in masonry for uplift) — follow AHJ. Do not pick a winner.

fastener_schedule.what: built-up girder face nails (AF&PA D5 variant)
fastener_schedule.pattern: two rows; plies vertical; joints over supports; adjacent joints ≥16 in apart
fastener_schedule.source: AF&PA Beams. D5 — do not mix with HUD 10d/12 on one beam. Follow NDS/IRC.

fastener_schedule.what: built-up girder face nails (HUD D5 variant)
fastener_schedule.pattern: staggered; butts at/near supports, staggered plies
fastener_schedule.source: HUD §5.4.3. D5 — do not mix with AF&PA 20d/32 on one beam. Follow NDS/IRC.

fastener_schedule.size: not named in extract (grid only; no brand)
fastener_schedule.pattern: panels long way across supports, ≥2 spans

layering: Sawn bearing ≥1½ in on wood/metal, ≥3 in on masonry (AF&PA). D10 — do not apply 1½ in under I-joists.
Crawl clearances 12 in earth-to-girder, 18 in earth-to-joist (AF&PA).
Sawn hole/notch: no holes/notches in middle third; outer-third notch ≤1/6 depth; end notch ≤1/4; hole ≤1/3 depth and ≥2 in from edges (AF&PA). Do not mix with I-joist tables.
code_to_check: HUD RSDG is an IRC companion. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. HUD prints no R502/R503 for floors (gap-sop-irc-section-numbers). Do not invent R502.
NDS 4.4.1 still wants ≥8 ft bridging on 2x10/2x12 (HUD §5.4.2 D3). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
APA AFG-01 glue recommended by AF&PA/HUD (squeaks/stiffness) — not the PJI catalog-span requirement. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
time_money: I-joist vs sawn is a permit-gate framing choice. Hole/notch and bearing rules do not swap between the two. No dollars in sources.
